# What we built

## What composable modelling would need

+-------------------------+------------------------------------------+
| Theme                   | What it would need                       |
+=========================+==========================================+
| Uncertainty and         | Propagate it properly, and swap the      |
| inference               | inference method                         |
+-------------------------+------------------------------------------+
| Model structure         | Separate infection, latent and           |
|                         | observation processes, and nest models   |
|                         | inside models                            |
+-------------------------+------------------------------------------+
| Population              | Stratify any component without hand      |
| heterogeneity           | managing the bookkeeping                 |
+-------------------------+------------------------------------------+
| Accessibility and       | Components carry their priors, work      |
| interoperability        | standalone, and talk to the rest of      |
|                         | Julia                                    |
+-------------------------+------------------------------------------+
| Workflow                | One specification for simulation and for |
|                         | inference                                |
+-------------------------+------------------------------------------+

::: {.attribution}
Table 1 of the paper sets out six themes, condensed to five rows here,
with accessibility and interoperability merged. In the paper each
design consideration is paired with the problem that motivates it.
These came from the authors and have had no community input
:::

## The proof of concept

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
- A thin language for epidemiology over a probabilistic backend that
  does the sampling
- Three component families. Infection, latent, and observation
  processes, composing across families and within them
- Components carry their own priors, so domain knowledge travels with
  the component rather than with the person
- Model definitions do not know about the data, so one definition
  simulates and fits

::: {.attribution}
Bullets three and four are design considerations from the previous
slide · Abbott et
al., *Composable probabilistic models can lower barriers to rigorous
infectious disease modelling*,
[doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17884675](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17884675)
:::
